R0041.title: Card Cracking
R0041.definition: Obtaining valid payment information by enumerating different missing start/expiry dates and security codes.
R0041.description: Brute-forcing the start/expiry dates and security codes (CSC) of payment cards, also known as CVN2, CVC, CV2, or CID. The results of a carding attack (R0040) can be used to assess payment card or account value, while successfully cracked payment-card security codes and expiry dates can be used for actual payments.
R0041.influence: Once attackers successfully enumerate payment card security codes, expiration dates, and other key payment information, they can use it for card fraud, black-card payments, account value screening, and follow-on financial fraud, causing cardholder losses, merchant chargeback losses, payment-channel risk controls, and damage to platform transaction reputation.

references.title: OWASP Automated Threat: OAT010 Card Cracking

observables: The payment endpoint receives multiple security code or expiry date enumeration requests for the same card number within a short window
The same payment card is repeatedly tried with different CVC and expiry date combinations across multiple merchant endpoints
The CVC or expiry date field values in payment requests exhibit enumeration sequences such as incrementing or decrementing patterns
The payment attempt failure rate for the same card number within a short window is abnormally high, with failures concentrated on security code errors
Multiple different card numbers initiate structurally similar payment enumeration requests from the same device or IP within a short window
